headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage/cascading error: Copilot can read repo context and write edits, while LightZero is read-only and non-networked, so the pair mainly risks unsafe code propagation rather than direct exfiltration.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Copilot can read editor buffers and repo context and propose edits, so malicious content in files could influence its outputs. LightZero has no filesystem or network I/O, so it cannot actively bridge or amplify injection. The pathway exists only through manual review/copying, making blast radius small.
conditions: IF a user pastes attacker-controlled text into Copilot-visible files or buffers
IF Copilot-generated edits are copied into LightZero prompts or training inputs
mitigations: Review any Copilot-suggested text before reuse
Keep untrusted content in separate files
Do not feed raw file contents from Copilot into LightZero prompts
Use a short prompt template that strips instructions
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to copied snippets

B_data_leakage.rationale: Copilot touches source code and open editor buffers and sends context to api.githubcopilot.com, but LightZero touches no data classes and has no egress. There is no shared workspace or secret-handling surface in LightZero, so leakage from the pair is limited to ordinary code-context exposure already implied by Copilot.
conditions: IF sensitive secrets are stored in files visible to Copilot
IF those files are opened in the editor while Copilot is active
mitigations: Remove secrets from open buffers
Use placeholder values in sample configs
Close sensitive files before invoking Copilot
Restrict Copilot to non-sensitive repositories
requires-engineering: enforce secret scanning before editor sync

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Copilot can write the filesystem and modify git state, but LightZero cannot read or write the filesystem, modify git state, or use network. With no overlapping mutable resource, there is no write-write conflict pathway between the pair.
conditions: IF LightZero is wrapped by an external orchestrator that grants it write access not shown in its profile
mitigations: Keep LightZero isolated from the repo workspace
Do not grant LightZero filesystem write permissions
Run Copilot Workspace changes through human review
requires-engineering: add OS-level sandboxing for any future LightZero wrapper

D_cascading_error.rationale: Copilot can generate code edits from repo context, and LightZero can be used as a downstream consumer of those outputs if an operator copies them into game-playing or benchmark code. LightZero does not verify provenance or correctness, so the pair can propagate mistaken code or assumptions, though no autonomous action-taking is shown.
conditions: IF Copilot-generated code is copied into LightZero-related scripts or configs
IF LightZero outputs are treated as authoritative without independent validation
mitigations: Manually test any copied code before use
Compare outputs against a second source
Keep a changelog of copied snippets
Require human approval for downstream edits
requires-engineering: add automated validation for imported code

E_compliance.rationale: Copilot is a closed-source GitHub/Microsoft service with GitHub repo OAuth context, while LightZero is open-source and touches no data classes. The pair does not show a residency or regulated-data mismatch by itself, but Copilot’s vendor-hosted processing can create compliance gaps if regulated code or data is opened in the editor.
conditions: IF regulated data is opened in Copilot-visible buffers
IF organizational policy forbids vendor-hosted processing of repository context
mitigations: Avoid opening regulated files in Copilot
Use a non-sensitive test repo
Check vendor policy before enabling Chat/Workspace
Document data-flow boundaries for the repo
requires-engineering: route regulated work to an approved local model
